jobs.occupation: PhD Candidate in Impacts of Balancing Market Design on Operational Costs and Market Prices
jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 8,6000 employees and 44,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

You will find more information about working at NTNU and the application process here.   
Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_KHQjc4ndas&t=41sAbout the position
Are you motivated to take a step towards a doctorate and open up exciting career opportunities? Do you have a background in electrical power engineering, operations research, or a related field, and are you interested in energy systems and markets? As a PhD candidate with us, you will work to achieve your doctorate, and at the same time gain valuable experience that qualifies you for a further career in higher education and research, both in and outside academia. 

The Department of Electric Energy (IEL) at NTNU is seeking a highly motivated candidate for a full-time (100%) PhD position for 3 years. You will join the research group Electricity Markets and Energy System Planning (EMESP) at IEL, where we foster an open, inclusive, and collaborative working environment.

Our work environment is defined by its friendly and supportive atmosphere, with regular gatherings such as professional meetings within the research group, weekly colloquia, shared lunches, and “Friday coffee” sessions to end the week. These formal and informal events offer opportunities to share ideas, celebrate milestones, and build relationships. PhD candidates also organize social activities open to everyone interested, fostering a welcoming and inclusive community.

Your immediate Line Manager will be the Head of Department.
About the project
The doctoral candidate is expected to investigate and develop optimization-based mathematical models for reserve procurement and balancing energy in liberalized electricity systems. Particular attention will be given to: i) the construction of market bids based on fundamental market models, in which the representation of non-convex cost components is important, and ii) the timing of reserve procurement, investigating the potential benefits of co-optimizing reserve procurement and wholesale energy. This research will involve mathematical programming, including modeling of the hydropower system and stochastic optimization methods. The models developed will be used to analyze how different market designs affect the costs and prices of procuring reserve capacity and delivering balancing energy. The work will also aim to provide insights that are relevant for the further development of efficient and well-functioning balancing markets. 

The PhD candidate will be hosted in the Electricity Markets and Energy Systems Planning (EMESP) group at the Department of Electric Energy, NTNU. The main supervisor will be Professor Arild Helseth, with co-supervision from experts in balancing markets and market design, including Professor Hossein Farahmand (NTNU) and Research Manager Stefan Jaehnert (SINTEF Energy). The Norwegian TSO Statnett will serve as a discussion partner in this project.
Duties of the position
• Carry out research of high quality within the framework described above
• Participate in activities of the EMESP research group
• Complete academic training consisting of coursework corresponding to a minimum 30 ECTS
• Contribute to publications in relevant journals and to popular science dissemination
• Participate in international activities such as conferences and/or research stays at foreign educational institutions 
Career-enhancing work, which is in addition to the research project and doctoral education, may be offered to a candidate who demonstrates clear motivation and ability for such work, and if the Department determines there is a need. Examples of career-enhancing work include, but are not limited to, contributing to teaching, laboratory and exercise teaching, supervision, and examination work within the employee's areas of competence. 

Be prepared for changes to your work duties after employment.
Required selection criteria
• You must have a relevant Master's degree in either electrical power engineering, control engineering, managerial economics with strong quantitative skills, or physics or mathematics with a specialization in operations research. Your course of study must correspond to a five-year Norwegian course, where 120 credits have been obtained at master's level. Master's students can apply, but the master's degree must be obtained and documented before starting the position and no later than august 2027.
• You must have a strong academic background from your previous studies and have an average grade from your Master's degree study, or equivalent education, which is equal to B or better compared to NTNU's grading scale. If you do not have letter grades from previous studies, you must have an equally good academic foundation. If you have a weaker grade background, you may be considered if you can document that you are particularly suitable for a PhD education, i.e., by having relevant work experience and/or published/publishable scientific papers.
• You must meet the requirements for admission to the Faculty's Doctoral Programme.
• You must have English language skills, both written and spoken, corresponding to the scale B2 in the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR). Applicants who are not native English speakers are encouraged to document their English language proficiency. This can be done through an approved English language test. One of the following test scores could be documented for this purpose: 
• TOEFL internet-based test (iBT) - Score equivalent to the B2 level: 79 - 101. 
• IELTS - Score equivalent to the B2 level: 5.5 - 6.0 
• Cambridge English - Score equivalent to the B2 level: 160 - 179.
• 
Further assessment of both written and oral English language skills, as well as the ability to communicate fluently, will be conducted throughout the selection process and during any interviews for all applicants.

PLEASE NOTE: For detailed information about what the application must contain, see paragraph “About the application”.

The appointment is to be made in accordance with NTNUs guidelines for recruitment positions and Regulations for the degrees philosophiae doctor (ph.d.) and philosophiae doctor (ph.d.) in artistic development work at the Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU) for general criteria for the position.
Preferred selection criteria
• Work and/or research experience in electricity markets, hydropower scheduling, energy system modeling, and operations research or optimization.
• Excellent programming and modeling skills, preferably in Julia, Python, or a similar programming language.
• Familiarity with Nordic or European balancing-market developments and TSO practices.
• English language skills, both written and spoken, corresponding to the scale C1 in the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR). See which scores are equivalent to the C1 level here.Personal characteristics
To complete a doctoral degree (PhD), the candidate is expected to: 

• demonstrate strong motivation, curiosity, and a learning-oriented mindset
• work independently, take initiative, and maintain good structure and discipline in their work
• communicate effectively and collaborate well with supervisors and peers
• show resilience and work constructively when facing challenges or setbacks
• demonstrate integrity and a strong sense of responsibility in their research conduct
Emphasis will be placed on personal and interpersonal qualities.
We offer
• An exciting job with an important mission in society
• Developing tasks in a strong and international professional environment
• Career guidance and follow-up during the PhD period
• Open and inclusive working environment with committed colleagues
• Social activities organized by PhD Students
• Weekly social gathering on Fridays (Friday coffee)
• Working capital that can be used to implement the project
• Mentor programme as a new employee at NTNU
• Favorable terms as a member of the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund (SPK)  
• Free Norwegian language training at a basic level (A2)
As a PhD Candidate at NTNU, you will have access to employee benefits.
Diversity
Diversity is a strength, and at NTNU we aim to be an employer that reflects the diversity in society and that makes use of the potential of the population's collective skills. Our vision is Knowledge for a better world and our values ​​are creative, critical, constructive and respectful. We believe that an organization that is equal, diverse, and gender-balanced is essential for us to achieve our goals. 

We strive to attract employees with different skills, life experiences and perspectives to contribute to even better problem solving of our societal mission in research and education. 

If you think this position is relevant and interesting, we encourage you to apply, regardless of gender, functional ability, and cultural background, or whether you have been out of work for a period of time.

At NTNU we want to increase the proportion of women in scientific positions. We have a number of measures to promote equality. 
Salary and conditions
In the position of PhD Candidate, code 1017, your gross salary will normally be NOK 580 000,- per annum depending on qualifications and seniority. A 2% statutory contribution to the State Pension Fund is deducted from the salary. 

The employment period is 3 years, with the possibility of an additional 3 to 12 months of employment related to career-enhancing activities. 

The option for career-enhancing work may be offered to a candidate who has clear motivation and ability for such work, and if the Department deems it necessary. This will be clarified with the candidate during and after any interview. 

If you cannot document skills in Norwegian, Swedish, or Danish at level A2 upon employment, NTNU offers the opportunity to take Norwegian courses corresponding to at least 15 credits. NTNU will facilitate this. 

For employment as a PhD Candidate, it is a prerequisite that you gain admission to the PhD programme in Electric Power Engineering within three months of your employment contract start date, and that you participate in an organized doctoral programme throughout the period of employment.

The nature of the work will, with a high degree of likelihood, involve the development of, or access to, assets and information that are considered particularly vulnerable to activities posing a security risk, and for which compelling security considerations apply. The selected candidate must therefore undergo an assessment of personal security suitability. In this context, verification of identity, academic transcripts, and other submitted documentation will also be conducted.

As an employee at NTNU, it is important that you keep yourself up to date with academic and organizational changes and adapt to them.

For the necessary professional and social interaction, it is a prerequisite that you are physically present and available to the institution on a daily basis.
About the application
The attachments (including a description of your scientific work) must accompany the application as these documents form the basis of the application assessment. The documents must be in English. 

• A cover letter where the applicant explains personal motivation, briefly summarizes scientific work, and describes how their background is a good fit (400 words/1 page).
• Project outline containing proposals for an overall description of research questions, theoretical perspectives, methodological design for the project, and progress plan (maximum 1500 words/4 pages, including references). This proposal shall neither be deemed final nor binding for the project.
• CV.
• If you have testimonials of work experience, submit them.
• Transcripts and diplomas for Bachelor's and Master's degrees. If you have not yet completed your Master's thesis, you must provide confirmation of your estimated submission date for the Master's thesis, or confirmation that your Master's thesis has been submitted.
• Applicants from universities outside Norway are asked to provide a diploma supplement or similar document that details the study program and grading system. Also, see the specific documentation requirements for education obtained outside Norway, applicable to certain regions or countries, here.  
• A copy of the Master's thesis. If you have recently submitted your Master's thesis, you are encouraged to include a draft of the thesis. Documentation of a completed Master's degree must be provided before assuming the position. 
• If you have publications or other relevant research work, submit them.
• You are encouraged to include documentation of English language proficiency if you are not a native speaker of English. 
• Name and contact information of three referees.
If all, or parts, of your education has been taken abroad, we also ask you to attach documentation of the scope and quality of your entire education, both Bachelor's and Master's education, in addition to other higher education. If your institution uses “diploma supplement” (normal for most European institutions), you must attach this. A description of the documentation required can also be found here. If you already have a statement from Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir), please attach this as well. 

Joint work will be considered. If it is difficult to identify your contribution to joint work, you must attach a brief description of your participation.

When assessing the best qualified, we emphasize necessary qualifications such as education, experience and personal suitability. Motivation for the position, ambitions, and potential for research will also count when assessing the candidates.NTNU recognizes a wide range of academic contributions and has committed itself to The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment and CoARA (responsible assessment of research and recognition of a greater breadth of academic contributions in accordance with NTNU's social mission).
General information
A public list of applicants with name, age, job title and municipality of residence is prepared after the application deadline. If you wish to be exempt from entry on the public applicant list, this must be justified. Assessment will be made in accordance with current legislation. You will be notified if the exemption is not granted.

If you think this position looks interesting and in line with your qualifications, you are welcome to apply.If you have any questions about the position, please contact Professor Arild Helseth by email at arild.helseth@ntnu.no. 

If you have any questions about the recruitment process, please contact executive officer Ida Marie Thomsen Olsen at ida.m.t.olsen@ntnu.no 

Application deadline: 06.01.2027

For practical information about working at NTNU, please visit this webpage.

jobs.occupation: Head of Warehouse
jobs.description:
We are looking for an experienced and hands-on Head of Warehouse to lead and develop our warehouse and material-flow operations in a growing production environment.

The role combines people leadership, operational management, inventory control, material planning, production support, and continuous improvement. You will be responsible for ensuring that materials and components are available at the right time and in the right quantity, while maintaining high standards of inventory accuracy, efficiency, quality, safety, and production support.

You will work closely with Production, Purchasing, Planning, Quality, Logistics, and Management to ensure a reliable and efficient flow of materials throughout the organization.

This is a hands-on leadership role where you will be expected to both lead the warehouse team and stay close to daily operations.

In this role you will be responsible for:
Warehouse Operations & Material Flow
• 
Lead and coordinate daily warehouse operations, including receiving, inspection, storage, picking, kitting, internal material supply, packing, and outbound shipments.

• 
Ensure efficient and reliable material flow between warehouse, production, testing, and other operational areas.

• 
Ensure materials and components are correctly identified, stored, handled, and supplied to production.

• 
Coordinate loading and unloading activities in accordance with safety requirements.

• 
Ensure finished products, materials, and equipment are correctly prepared and documented for shipment.

• 
Develop and maintain an organized, efficient, and scalable warehouse structure.
Inventory Management
• 
Take overall responsibility for inventory accuracy and stock control.

• 
Establish and maintain routines for cycle counting, stock checks, reconciliation, and investigation of discrepancies.

• 
Monitor stock levels and proactively identify potential shortages or supply risks.

• 
Follow up on damaged, obsolete, or slow-moving inventory.

• 
Ensure all warehouse transactions and material movements are correctly registered in the ERP/WMS system.

• 
Develop and improve inventory-control processes as the company grows.
Production Planning & Material Supply
• 
Work closely with Production and Planning to ensure materials and components are available according to production requirements.

• 
Support production planning through accurate information on stock levels, material availability, and lead times.

• 
Develop and maintain efficient parts-kitting processes, ensuring production orders receive the correct components and quantities.

• 
Establish and improve material replenishment processes, including Kanban and pull-based systems where appropriate.

• 
Identify and resolve material-flow issues that may affect production.
ERP, Systems & Reporting
• 
Take ownership of warehouse-related processes and data in the ERP/WMS system.

• 
Ensure accurate receiving, issuing, transfers, picking, stock control, packing, shipping, and documentation.

• 
Use warehouse and inventory data to monitor performance and support operational decision-making.

• 
Establish relevant warehouse KPIs and follow up on performance.

• 
Support the implementation and development of warehouse systems, tools, and processes.
You have:
• 
Several years of progressive experience in warehouse management, inventory control, materials management, logistics, or a related field.

• 
Previous experience in a warehouse leadership or supervisory role.

• 
Experience from a manufacturing, industrial, engineering, or technically complex production environment is highly desirable.

• 
Strong practical experience with receiving, storage, picking, kitting, inventory management, material handling, and shipping.

• 
Experience supporting production planning and material requirements.

• 
Strong understanding of inventory control, stock accuracy, cycle counting, reconciliation, and replenishment.

• 
Practical experience with Kanban, pull systems, lean material flow, or similar replenishment processes is an advantage.

• 
Strong experience with ERP/WMS systems and warehouse data.

• 
Experience using data and KPIs to monitor and improve warehouse performance.

• 
Experience developing warehouse procedures, routines, and work instructions.

• 
Experience with 5S, continuous improvement, or lean principles is an advantage.

• 
Good forklift experience; T1, T2, and T4 certification is an advantage.

• 
Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

• 
Ability to prioritize and make decisions in a fast-paced production environment.

• 
English — fluent or strong professional working level.

• 
Ukrainian/Norwegian — an advantage.
What We Offer
• 
An opportunity to join a growing technology company at an exciting stage of development

• 
Meaningful responsibility and direct impact on products and processes

• 
A collaborative and international working environment

• 
Professional development and career growth opportunities

• 
Competitive compensation and benefits package

We review applications on an ongoing basis and encourage interested candidates to apply as soon as possible.

About the position
We invite applications for a Researcher position in computational chemistry, available at the Hylleraas centre, Department of Chemistry.

The position is for a period of 2 years.

Starting date no later than 01.03.2027.

Place of work is Hylleraas centre, Department of Chemistry at Blindern, Oslo.
Project description
The position is funded by the Research Council of Norway through the Researcher Project for Early Career Scientists (FRIPRO) “APExModel: Addressing Antimicrobial Peptides by Integrating Experiments into Modelling” and lead by Henrique Musseli Cezar. 

Antimicrobial resistance is a critical global health crisis, and new drugs are urgently needed. 

APExModel will establish a set of experimentally-grounded design principles that can aid the development of safer and more effective AMPs. This will be done by developing and applying a new computational framework that integrates experimental data into simulations. The project will also provide: 1) better understanding the molecular mechanisms that govern how AMPs self-assemble in solution, a key factor for their stability and activity; 2) a novel simulation methodology that can accurately model AMPs interacting with cell membranes by using experimental small-angle scattering data to guide the simulations; and 3) insights on the action mechanisms of different AMPs and how they disrupt bacterial membranes.

The most critical R&D challenge is the development of this new simulation methodology. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations provide access to dynamics at atomic resolution, but limitations in simulation timescale and accuracy may compromise the agreement with experiments. Current integrative approaches are limited to systems with spherical symmetry and cannot adequately model the flat, patch-like membrane used in most MD simulations of AMP-membrane studies. This project will overcome this limitation, adding a capability that is currently missing in the field.

Combining expertise from chemistry, pharmacy, and physics, this interdisciplinary project will produce a new open-source simulation tool and the fundamental knowledge required to establish design principles for AMPs.

jobs.description:
The opportunity
You'll design the tools that get groceries onto millions of doorsteps: not what shoppers see, but the systems used by people working in logistics operations at our fulfillment centers.

Oda’s mission is to build the world’s most efficient retail system, so people have space for life. A huge part of that is our sophisticated fulfillment and delivery system, designed and built entirely by us. It packs and delivers nearly half a million items every day to around 80.000 homes and businesses across Norway and Sweden. What we’ve built is second-to-none in the world when it comes to efficiency, and it’s held together by internal tools and processes that make the jobs of operators and drivers easy, fast, ergonomic, and smooth. That's where you come in.

You'll work in close collaboration with our colleagues in both Norway and at our sister company Mathem in Stockholm, and you’ll help us on the path to launching Oda Systems in new markets as we find customers who want to work with us to bring the most efficient solution for online groceries to more parts of the world.

The role
Service/UX designers play a major part in the design of our processes and tooling. Great processes are as much about ergonomics, workflow, physical space, team structures, and incentives as they are about screens. You’ll get the chance to not only work on software solutions but also consider how digital experiences should best interact with hardware/machinery, the physical space they’re situated in, and last but not least the operator routines around them. That combination is what makes logistics design at Oda different from most UX roles: you're never just designing a screen, you're designing a multi-dimensional workflow.

You’ll join the Delivery team within Oda’s Logistics platform, which is responsible for everything that happens out on the road. You’ll design the best possible experience for employees working with everything from capacity and route planning to traffic coordination, delivering groceries to customers, and leaders following up drivers and operations. While we’re happy with today’s processes, we’re not satisfied: there is a ton to be done to make things more efficient, more automated, and smarter, so that we have even better control over capacity, drivers have a better workday, and customers get their food on time and in full.

You'll work embedded in a cross-functional team, closely collaborating with other disciplines – Product Management, Engineering, Data and Insight, and Logistics development. This is a hands-on, office-based role. You'll be at our Fulfillment Center in Lier regularly, and at our Tøyen office most of the week (most of the team is at Tøyen at least 3 days a week). You’ll use AI actively in your processes, and contribute to driving agentic UX forwards.

What you'll do in Oda
• 
Lead big projects from start to finish: own them from the initial idea through concept, design, prototyping, implementation, testing, and follow-up after launch, working closely with your product team, as well as stakeholders in Logistics. You should feel comfortable putting on the PM hat and driving projects.

• 
Conduct UX research and data analysis: observe what’s going on in operations, run workshops with your team and stakeholders, look at the data, gather feedback in operations.

• 
Communicate and present your work to peers as well as stakeholders, showing your process, and the impact of your designs.

• 
Map and model complex, systemic workflows.

• 
Design user interfaces and build prototypes. You don’t have to be a pixel perfectionist, but you will draw screens. Prototype in Figma, or directly in code – whatever’s the fastest way to test an idea, with room to ship and test changes in production alongside developers.

• 
Work closely with teammates and stakeholders all the way from ideation to roll-out, rather than handing off at the end of a solo-design process.

• 
Contribute to setting the direction of the Delivery team, which determines its own projects based on company strategy

• 
Work with other designers to spar, give feedback, and build a stronger design community across Oda.

What we're looking for 🌟
• 
At least 8 years of experience in UX, interaction, or service design, in-house or agency, with a portfolio showing full ownership from insight to shipped product

• 
A full-stack design attitude: insight, concept, structure, and visual design, without waiting for handovers. Being open to being hands-on both on the warehouse floor and in our codebase.

• 
Very solid fundamentals in product sense and design: demonstrated insight-centric process, root cause analysis, work framed in desired outcomes, ability to distill complexity.

• 
Speed over perfection: You understand the importance of shipping fast, learning, and iterating over polishing a "perfect" blueprint. You leverage the advantage we have with having short feedback loops with our end-users.

• 
A track record of driving process change: not just shipping a solution, but bringing the operators who'll use it along with you.

• 
You already use AI as part of your own design process: you're genuinely interested in an AI-enhanced product development workflow, not just AI features bolted onto Figma.

• 
Fluent English. Intermediate Norwegian or Swedish is a strong plus, since you'll be working directly with traffic coordinators, drivers, and leaders on-site.

• 
Previous logistics experience is a plus, not a requirement.

What we offer 🚀
• 
A flexible schedule built around a healthy work-life balance.

• 
Modern, empowered product teams: democratized data access, good tools, a sustainable pace. We ship, and you will immediately see the impact of your work.

• 
A team that's actively working AI into both design and development, not just talking about it, and genuinely open to designers who want to prototype or write code.

• 
A design community across all Oda teams: UX design, Service design, Digital design, UX research, Content design, and Graphic design.

• 
A culture that values kindness, transparency, and taking action over process for its own sake.

• 
A modern office at Tøyen with an amazing subsidized canteen by Naked Lunch, bike parking, and a great rooftop terrace.

You'll be working with people who are ambitious about logistics in a way most designers never get to be. Come build the future with us!

jobs.description:
About the position
We invite applications for a full-time position as Associate Professor in cell biology at the Section for Physiology and Cell Biology, Department of Biosciences, Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences, University of Oslo.

The Department of Biosciences seeks an active researcher with a strong publication record within cell biology. The successful applicant should be on an upward trajectory and have strong potential to develop and execute research projects at a high international level. The research should address fundamental questions in cell biology using animal- or plant-based systems and create synergies with current research in the section and department. 

Research in the Section for Physiology and Cell Biology includes physiological adaptations to extreme conditions, comparative immunology, muscle physiology, neural mechanisms of learning and memory in health and disease, plant signalling and development, cellular and molecular mechanisms of disease including stress signalling, hormone action and cancer biology, as well as intracellular membrane trafficking, organelle dynamics, and mechanisms regulating cell migration and organization. The research groups develop and apply advanced technologies including live imaging, molecular tools and gene engineering, omics technologies and bioinformatics.

The Department of Biosciences is organized into four research sections; Section for Physiology and Cell biology (FYSCELL), Section for Environmental and marine biology (EMB), Section for, Ecology, Biodiversity, and Evolution (EBE), and Section for Molecular Biology, Biochemistry and Bioinformatics (MBB). The research at the department focuses on fundamental biological processes from the molecular and cellular level to the population and ecosystem level. The department has recently moved into the new Life Science Building, which brings together researchers and students from chemistry, pharmacy, biosciences and laboratory medicine and provides state-of-the-art research infrastructure. The department provides access to advanced research infrastructure, including state-of-the-art core facilities, field stations, and specialized platforms that support interdisciplinary life science research across multiple disciplines.
Your main tasks will be
• Develop and lead an internationally competitive research programme in cell biology, using animal- or plant-based systems and taking advantage of existing infrastructure and common research facilities.
• Secure external research funding and establish or contribute to national and international research collaborations and initiatives.
• Carry out research-based teaching in cell biology and molecular biology at bachelor´s, master´s and PhD levels, including laboratory-based courses and supervise master’s and PhD students.
• Contribute to the academic development of the section and department through collegial activities, scientific leadership, and administrative duties.What skills are important in this role?

• Documented experience in securing external research funding.
• Applicants must document academic qualifications in cell biology equivalent to an Associate Professor position. Scientific qualifications will be given significant weight, with particular emphasis on the quality and extent of scientific output within cell biology over the last five years, as well as experience with modern experimental research methods and techniques.
• The successful applicant must be able to carry out research-based teaching in cell and molecular biology at bachelor, master and PhD levels including laboratory-based courses and supervise Master and PhD students.

• Focus on student learning

Candidates who do not have sufficient mastery of a Scandinavian language (B2 level) at the time of appointment, will be required attain B2 level proficiency in Norwegian within three years of employment.
Desired qualifications:

• The person appointed will be requested to take on some administrative duties. Hence such experience will be an advantage.
• Experience in utilizing advanced research infrastructure such as those available at the Department of Biosciences and the University of Oslo, and the ability to contribute to their further development, is an advantage.What are we looking for in you?
Personal skills:

• Ability to create and contribute to a well-functioning, inclusive and productive research environment
• Networking skills, ability to collaborate and conduct scientific leadership
• Ability to cooperate and communicate well with other members of staff
The successful candidate should have an international profile consistent with to the above criteria. The candidate will be selected based on documented qualifications and the fit and expertise to strengthen and create synergies with the research profiles of the section and department.
We can offer you

• Committed colleagues in a good working environment.

jobs.description:
This is NTNU
NTNU is a broad-based university with a technical-scientific profile and a focus in professional education. The university is located in three cities with headquarters in Trondheim.

At NTNU, 9,000 employees and 43,000 students work to create knowledge for a better world.

Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WWHqR5i1FHE&feature=youtu.beAbout the Job
The Department of Information Security and Communication Technology (IIK) at NTNU Gjøvik has a vacancy for a Researcher in Socio-Technical Fraud Systems. 

The position is for an intended period of 24 months and is part of SAFE – Secure Anti-Fraud Excellence Center, funded by Sparebankstiftelsen Hedmark and SpareBank 1 Østlandet in collaboration with NTNU and industry partners.The researcher will be a key member of WP1 and lead its socio-technical root cause analysis of financial fraud, hosted at CCIS, NTNU Gjøvik. WP1 examines vishing and safe-account fraud from both the attacker and the victim perspective and a proposed extension to investment fraud. It distinguishes technical authentication and payment confirmation from legally valid consent.

The research reconstructs how fraud unfolds across channels, while focusing detection and intervention on evidence actually visible to the bank between customer authentication and payment authorisation. Off-bank calls, screen sharing and remote-access activities are described where case sources support them, but are not assumed to be observable by the bank.

The work draws on public decisions of Finansklagenemnda, court judgments, and anonymised or otherwise lawfully accessible cases from SAFE’s banking partners. Results feed into cognitive experiments (WP2), detection research (WP3), scientific publications and a policy white paper.Center for Cyber and Information Security (CCIS) at NTNU will host the SAFE Project.Your immediate leader is head of department.
Duties of the position
• Build a systematically coded corpus of fraud cases from public decisions and lawfully accessible bank material, using a shared template and a cross-channel timeline.
• Develop evidence-based fraud scripts for vishing and safe-account fraud and, subject to scope confirmation, investment fraud, including interim inputs for WP2.
• Map each fraud stage, the channels involved, signs of real-time guidance, and what is actually observable by the bank between authentication and payment authorisation.
• Identify legitimate customer activities with similar bank-visible patterns, to support realistic false-alarm testing without using victim characteristics as automatic detection features.
• Study intervention points and fraudster adaptation, including cases where the bank suspects fraud but the customer rejects warnings; help plan a tabletop session with a banking partner.
• Analyse legal, ethical and governance conditions for collecting, using and sharing fraud-related signals, including privacy, bank confidentiality and interbank cooperation.
• Examine the conditions for transaction warnings, delays, refusals and escalation, with attention to customer consent, liability and loss allocation.
• Assess payee verification and, in investment-fraud cases, checks of providers against Finanstilsynet’s register and market warnings; distinguish these from bank-account verification.
• Provide fraud scripts and realistic look-alike scenarios to WP2 and observability findings, intervention points and lawful-signal constraints to WP3.
• Prepare WP1 deliverables, scientific publications and a policy white paper, and present findings to the SAFE Advisory Board and project partners.
• Contribute, where relevant, to SAFE continuing education (EVU), project reporting and research proposal development.Required selection criteria
• A master’s degree (120 ECTS or equivalent) or a PhD in information security, socio-technical systems, criminology, information systems, law and technology, or a closely related field.
• Documented experience with systematic analysis of qualitative material, such as case files, legal decisions, interviews or incident reports, using a coding scheme or structured method.
• Knowledge of social engineering and fraud in digital channels, such as vishing, authorised push payment fraud or investment fraud.
• Understanding of digital banking and payment processes, including authentication, payment initiation and customer interaction channels.
• Ability to recognise legal, ethical and data-protection questions and work with relevant specialists on their implications for fraud prevention research.
• Reading comprehension of Norwegian or another Scandinavian language sufficient to analyse Norwegian case material and legal decisions.
• Good written and spoken English and the ability to prepare clear, well-structured research reports.Preferred selection criteria
• A PhD in a relevant field, or research experience after completion of the master’s degree.
• Experience in applied research projects involving banks, financial crime specialists or regulatory and legal experts.
• Experience in crime script analysis, situational crime prevention, socio-technical analysis, or process and threat modelling.
• Knowledge of Norwegian or EU rules on payment services, data protection, bank confidentiality or financial crime prevention.
• Experience in fraud prevention, anti-money laundering, compliance or incident handling in the financial sector.
• Experience in planning and facilitating interviews, workshops or tabletop exercises with practitioners.
• Relevant scientific publications or reports on fraud, cybercrime or socio-technical security.
• Skills in structuring and analysing data, for example using Python, R or NVivo.
• Spoken Norwegian or another Scandinavian language for cooperation with partner banks.Personal characteristics
• Highly motivated for applied and collaborative research with financial-sector partners.
• Analytical, structured and precise in the handling of research evidence and sources.
• Discreet and reliable in handling confidential case material and working across disciplines.
• Self-driven, communicative and able to deliver to agreed deadlines.
• Personal suitability will be emphasized.We offer
• Exciting and stimulating research tasks in a strong international academic environment
• Active collaboration with leading industrial and research partners in Norway and abroad.
• A professional and inclusive work environment.
• Favorable terms in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund
• Employee benefits at NTNUSalary and conditions

About the application

jobs.occupation: PhD Research Fellow in maps and models for nature in land-use planning
jobs.description:
Western Norway University of Applied Sciences (HVL) has a vacancy for a PhD Research Fellow in maps and models for nature in land-use planning
About the position:

The PhD Research Fellow will join the Landscape, Ecology and Climate research group at the Department of Civil Engineering and Environmental Sciences, at the Sogndal campus. The position is funded through the national research center Landfutures, as part of its research area "Maps and models". The position is a fixed-term, four year position with 25 % career-enhancing work at the department. The candidate will be enrolled in the PhD program Responsible Innovation and Regional Development at HVL.  Planned start date is Q1 of 2027.
About the PhD project/ work tasks:
About LandfuturesLandfutures is an eight-year research center for sustainable land and nature use (2026– 2034), funded by the Research Council of Norway. The center is led by Western Norway Research Institute and run jointly with Western Norway University of Applied Sciences, the Norwegian Mapping Authority (Kartverket), the Institute of Transport Economics, Nordland Research Institute, Ruralis, the Norwegian Computing Center and the Basque Center for Climate Change. Landfutures focuses on interests, values and practices in planning, with special attention to the regional level, and works closely with county authorities, county governors and municipalities.

Background and research needLand-use change is the main driver of biodiversity loss in Norway, and most decisions about land use outside protected areas are made in municipal land-use planning. At the core of these decisions is usually a map: which areas are most valuable for biodiversity, and where would development do the least harm? Yet mapping of nature is patchy, and although new nationwide data products such as the planned "Naturkart" are on the way, data alone do not tell a planner what to do. Municipalities can calculate the greenhouse-gas emissions of land-use change, but biodiversity has no currency comparable to tonnes of carbon dioxide Project-level methods such as "Naturkompasset" are emerging, but no spatially explicit tool supports strategic, plan-level choices about where to build. Systematic conservation planning offers  principles for such a tool: explicit targets, complementary areas, minimum cost and transparent trade-offs. Mature software exists (e.g. prioritizr, Zonation, Marxan), but the approach is hardly used in Norwegian planning. Different targets, data and methods can also point to different places on the map, and how far professionals agree on where nature matters most is an open question. 

Possible research directionsThe PhD project addresses one overarching question: How can maps and models give robust, transparent recommendations that professionals can agree on, about where to build and where to safeguard nature? We see three broad areas in which the thesis can contribute. The examples are meant to show the range of possibilities, not a fixed work plan. 

1. Practice – how plans and assessment methods treat nature today. What do existing planning documents and assessment methods actually map, prioritize and assume? Examples: how municipal biodiversity plans ("kommunedelplaner for naturmangfold") reflect principles from conservation biology and landscape ecology, such as complementarity and connectivity; or how new methods for assessing nature loss in development projects, such as "Naturkompasset", are structured and used.

2. Tools – spatial prioritization and how sensitive the answers are. Which planning needs can be formulated as spatial optimization problems, and how robust are the resulting recommendations? Examples: using systematic conservation planning at county scale to support plan revision ("planvask" – reviewing outdated zoning for development) or coordination across municipal borders; testing how much priority maps or impact scores change with different input data, criteria or assumptions about ecosystem condition.

3. Uncertainty and agreement – where experts and data diverge, and where new knowledge pays off. How large is professional disagreement about priority areas, and where would better data change the decision? Examples: how similar the priority maps are when independent groups of experts solve the same planning task; or identifying locations where additional field surveys in environmental impact assessments would be most likely to change a planning decision. 

The thesis will be article-based, comprising 3–4 scientific papers. Their exact scope, cases and methods will be developed together with the supervisors, and we expect the candidate to shape at least one of them from their own ideas (see Application below). User partners in Landfutures offer opportunities to work with real planning processes and cases. 

Research environmentThe PhD Research Fellow will be part of the Landscape, Ecology and Climate research group in Sogndal, an interdisciplinary group of ecologists and social scientists. The supervision team is Associate Professor Julien Vollering and Professor Inger Auestad, with the opportunity to involve additional supervisors where needed. Through Landfutures, the candidate will work with research partners such as the Norwegian Mapping Authority and the Norwegian Computing Center. User partners include seven county authorities, four county governors, and municipalities through the Norwegian Association of Local and Regional Authorities (KS). The center is recruiting four PhD candidates and three postdocs with different disciplinary backgrounds, and there are opportunities for exchange with complementary PhD projects within and outside Landfutures. The research fellow will recieve a fixed annual stipend to cover necessary expenses, such as participation in conferences/workshops/training or purchase of services/licenses/equipment.

Teaching duties would likely be in courses such as landscape ecology, GIS, or spatial planning.
Qualifications:
Criteria for appointment to the position of Phd Research Fellow are regulated in Forskrift til universitets- og høyskoleloven.

Required qualifications:

• A Master’s degree (120 ECTS) in ecology, conservation biology, physical or human geography, environmental or natural resource management, climate change management, land-use planning, landscape architecture, or a closely related field
• Grade B or better on the Master’s thesis and grade C or better on average in the Master’s degree (ECTS scale or equivalent)
• Documented experience with GIS and spatial data analysis
• Documented experience with R or another programming language for data analysis, such as Python
• Minimum B1 level in Norwegian or another Scandinavian language, and minimum B2 level in English (CEFR)
The following qualifications will be considered advantageous:

• Familiarity with Norwegian land-use planning or nature management, for example through work experience
• Experience with spatial prioritization or statistical modeling of spatial data
• Experience with R specifically (if your programming experience is in another language)
• B2 level or higher in Norwegian and C1 level or higher in English (CEFR)
We are looking for someone who: 

• is curious, analytical and comfortable working with varied map data
• works well both independently and together with researchers and practitioners from other disciplines
Applicants should explicitly address the qualifications listed above in their application, and provide documentation supporting them. 

Admission to the PhD programme

An application for admission to the programme should be submitted only after employment has been secured. Normally, an application for admission to the PhD programme must be submitted within 3 months of the start date. See Section 2-4 of the Regulations for the Degree of PhD at HVL. The research fellow must be admitted to the PhD programme no later than 3 months after the commencement of their employment. Further information about the PhD programme can be found at https://www.hvl.no/en/research/phd-programmes/.

Career plan

The person appointed must, in conjunction with the department, prepare a career plan that specifies the competences the fellow is to acquire. Competence goals must be set for both the doctoral work and any other career-enhancing work that is added to the position. The fellow will have access to career guidance. Other career-enhancing work may, for example, include teaching and teaching-related work, acquiring Norwegian language skills, contributions to research communities, collaboration with public or private actors, and more.

Background check

For available positions, HVL conducts background checks on applicants in collaboration with an external supplier, to verify information that appears from available documents. Background checks are always carried out with the candidate's consent, and employment in these positions requires a completed background check.
Application procedure:
Applications will be evaluated by an expert panel of three members.

Applicants are asked to submit their application and CV online. Please use the link “Apply for this job” (“Søk stillingen”).

The following documentation should be uploaded as an attachment to the online application: 

• Research Sketch (max. 1 page, 500 words) describing a paper you would like to pursue within the research area: the question, why it matters, and how it could be answered. The sketch will be assessed on relevance, originality and feasibility. It is not binding – its purpose is to show how you think. The sketch may be written in English or Norwegian; references do not count toward the page limit.
• Diplomas and certificates
• Master Thesis
• If any, copies of selected academic publications (no more than 15)
• A CV with a complete list of academic publications
Applicants should indicate which publications or parts of publications should be given special consideration in the evaluation. If the documents submitted are not in a Scandinavian language or in English, the applicants must submit certified translations of these. The transcripts must specify the topics, the course works, and the grades at the bachelor`s and master`s degree levels.

Applicants with a degree from a country other than Norway, need to attach a certified translation of the diploma and transcripts of grades to English or a Scandinavian language, in addition to the original documents, if the original is not in any of these languages. It is required that the applicant encloses a recognition document showing that their degree is equivalent to a Norwegian bachelor’s degree, master’s degree, or PhD. You can read more about applying for recognition of foreign higher education here.

The Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir) offers an automatic recognition document for certain degrees from selected countries. If the applicant’s degree is covered by the automatic recognition, it will be sufficient to attach this document. Read more about automatic recognition here.

As the HK-dir application process may take some time it is recommended to apply to HK-dir as soon as possible. If you have not received a recognition document from HK- dir within the application deadline, please enclose documentation from HK-dir showing that they have received your application.

Applicants should note that the evaluation will be based on the documentation submitted electronically via Jobbnorge within the submission deadline. The applicants are responsible for ensuring that all the documentation is submitted before the closing date. It is of utmost importance that all publications to be considered in the evaluation are uploaded as an attachment with the application, since these are sent electronically to the expert panel. Applications cannot be sent by e-mail or to individuals at the college.
General information:
The appointment will be made in accordance with the regulations for State employees Law in Norway ("Lov om statens ansatte"). Organizational changes and changes in the duties and responsibilities associated with the position must be expected.

State employment shall reflect the multiplicity of the population at large to the highest possible degree. Western Norway University of Applied Sciences therefore aims to achieve a balanced age and gender composition and the recruitment of persons with diverse backgrounds.

Information about the applicants may be made public even though the applicant has requested not to be named in the list of applicants. The applicant will be notified if his/her request is not respected.

Short-listed applicants will be called in for an interview. 

Employment is on condition that you are granted a work and residence permit (considered individually).

Western Norway University of Applied Sciences is subjected to the regulation for export control system. The regulation will be applied in the processing of the applications.
Salary:
• Good occupational pension, insurance and loan schemes from The Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund
• Exciting academic environment with the possibility of competence enhancement and development
• Opportunities for training within the working hours  
The PhD Research Fellow position is compensated according to position code 1017 Research Fellow, with a starting salary of NOK 568.700,-. Automatic salary progression is provided for up to 4 years, with an annual increase of 3%. 

There is a compulsory 2 % deduction to the pension fund (see http://www.spk.no for more information). The successful applicant must comply with the guidelines that apply to the position at any time.
Contacts:
1) Inger Auestad, Professor -  + 47 57676222 / email: inger.auestad@hvl.no

3) Liv Norunn Hamre, Assistant head of department - +47 57676229 / email: liv.hamre@hvl.no
 
2. Julien Vollering, Associate Professor - email: julien.vollering@hvl.no

Om arbeidsgiveren:

With about 16, 500 students, Western Norway University of Applied Sciences is one of the largest higher education institutions in Norway. A broad range of academic programmes are offered at Bachelor, Master and PhD levels, spread out on five campuses Førde, Sogndal, Bergen, Stord og Haugesund.

Our ambition is to build stronger and more solid academic and research environments that will interact nationally and internationally. The aim is to become a recognized actor on the international higher education arena. Increased international cooperation and engagement in externally funded projects will work towards this goal.

We cooperate with many national and international research groups, and with national and regional industry partners.

The department has around 900 students and more than 80 staff members and plays a key role in advancing the green transition through research and education in sustainable infrastructure, land use, and nature restoration.

jobs.occupation: Stipendiat i forhistorisk arkeologi
jobs.description:
Om stillingen
Universitetet i Stavanger har ledig stilling som stipendiat i forhistorisk arkeologi ved Arkeologisk museum, Avdeling for konservering. Stillingen er ledig fra 1.mars 2027.

Stipendiatstillingen leder frem til en doktorgrad og gir deg mulighet til å utvikle forskningskompetanse i et aktivt og stimulerende fagmiljø. Gjennom doktorgradsutdanningen vil du tilegne deg kunnskaper, ferdigheter og erfaring som kvalifiserer for videre karriere innen forskning, høyere utdanning og andre kunnskapsintensive sektorer.

Den som ansettes vil bli tatt opp på ph.d.-programmet i Samfunnsvitenskap. Programmet omfatter blant annet selvstendig forskningsarbeid, deltakelse i nasjonale og internasjonale forskermiljø samt forskningsformidling. Les mer om forskerutdanningen ved UiS på våre nettsider.
 
Stillingen er for tre år med ren forskerutdanning. 

Som stipendiat ved UiS får du støtte til faglig og karrieremessig utvikling gjennom veiledning, kompetanseutvikling og karriereplanlegging.

Stillingen er eksternt finansiert gjennom prosjektet «TRACES: Tracking Rock Art and oChre EnvironmentS», som er finansiert av Norges forskningsråd (NFR).
Forskningstema
TRACES undersøker forhistorisk bruk av oker, teknologi knyttet til bergkunst og samspillet mellom mennesker og miljø i Nord-Norge gjennom forhistorisk tid. Pigmenter og bergmalerier representerer noen av menneskehetens tidligste symbolske uttrykkssystemer og gir innsikt i menneskelig kommunikasjon, identitet og tilknytning gjennom tusenvis av år.

Prosjektets hovedhypotese er at felles teknologiske nettverk bidro til å opprettholde kulturelle og sosiale tradisjoner i perioder med omfattende klimatiske endringer. Sentrale forskningsspørsmål er blant annet:

• Hvilke strategier ble benyttet for anskaffelse av oker, og hvordan var mobilitets- og utvekslingsnettverkene knyttet til oker organisert i forhistorisk Norge?
• Hvordan varierte disse nettverkene over tid og mellom ulike regioner?
• I hvilken grad kan koblinger mellom pigmenter på udaterte bergmalerier og daterte arkeologiske kontekster bidra til å etablere et materialbasert kronologisk rammeverk?
• Hvordan tilpasset forhistoriske jeger-sankergrupper sine teknologiske systemer og symbolske nettverk seg til store miljø- og klimaendringer?
Stipendiatens rolleStipendiaten skal forske på arkeologiske okersamlinger og forhistoriske pigmentteknologier i Norge. Datagrunnlaget vil bli utviklet gjennom studier av museumsamlinger, publisert forskning og grå litteratur, ikke-destruktive spektroskopiske analyser i felt, geokjemiske laboratorieundersøkelser samt eksperimentell rekonstruksjon av forhistoriske malingoppskrifter og pigmentnettverk.

Den som ansettes vil utforske, anvende og kombinere ulike analytiske tilnærminger og metoder, herunder:

• katalogisering av museums-samlinger og gjenstander
• gjennomføring av geokjemiske analyser
• bruk av multivariate statistiske metoder
• planlegging og gjennomføring av workshops innen eksperimentell arkeologi 
Erfaring fra ett eller flere av disse områdene er en fordel. Søkere med erfaring fra arkeometriske analysemetoder, for eksempel SEM-EDS, (p)XRF, XRD, Raman-spektroskopi eller LA-ICP-MS, vil bli foretrukket. Opplæring i relevante metoder vil bli gitt ved behov.

Stipendiaten forventes å utvikle ny kunnskap som bidrar både til egen faglig kompetanseutvikling og til prosjektets samlede målsettinger. Stipendiaten vil inngå som en sentral del av prosjektgruppen og delta aktivt i prosjektets ulike aktiviteter, inkludert møter, workshops, vitenskapelig formidling og publisering.

Det oppfordres også til at stipendiaten gjennomfører et forskningsopphold ved Archaeometry Laboratory ved University of Missouri Research Reactor (MURR), USA, i løpet av stipendiatperioden.
Prosjektskisse
Som søker skal du utarbeide en foreløpig prosjektskisse ( 3-5 sider) for et doktorgradsprosjekt innenfor det beskrevne forskningstemaet.

Prosjektskissen skal redegjøre for forskningsproblemstillingen, dens relevans, samt den foreslåtte teoretiske og metodiske tilnærmingen. Skissen vil inngå i kompetansevurderingen.

Dersom du blir ansatt, vil prosjektskissen og prosjektets framdriftsplan videreutvikles i samarbeid med veilederne i løpet av de tre første månedene av ansettelsesperioden og danne grunnlag for den endelige planen for doktorgradsprosjektet. Mal for prosjektskisse finner du her.
Kvalifikasjoner
Du må ha sterk faglig bakgrunn med en femårig mastergrad i arkeologi, konservering, arkeometri, arkeologisk vitenskap, kulturarvvitenskap, geovitenskap, konserveringsvitenskap eller et nært beslektet fagområde, eller tilsvarende kvalifikasjoner som gir grunnlag for opptak til doktorgradsutdanning. Det er en fordel at graden er avlagt nylig.

Karakteren på masteroppgaven og det vektede gjennomsnittet for mastergraden må begge tilsvare karakteren B eller bedre.

Dersom du har utdanning fra en institusjon med annen karakterskala enn A-F, ber vi deg legge ved dokumentasjon som viser hvordan karakterene kan sammenliknes med den norske karakterskalaen. Du kan bruke disse konverteringsskalaene til å beregne poengene dine for opptak.
 
Vi vil også legge vekt på om du:

• viser høy faglig integritet og en sterk forpliktelse til kvalitet i arbeidet ditt
• er nysgjerrig og motivert for å gjennomføre forskningsprosjektet og bidra til faglige fellesskap og tverrfaglig samarbeid
• har et godt forskningspotensial innen fagområdet og de personlige egenskapene som kreves for å fullføre doktorgradsutdanningen innen ansettelsesperioden
• evner å arbeide effektivt både selvstendig og i samarbeid med andre forskere
• viser evne til kritisk refleksjon, innovativ tenkning og selvstendig problemløsning, samt arbeider strukturert og målrettet
• har gode samarbeids- og kommunikasjonsevner og bidrar til et konstruktivt arbeidsmiljø
• behersker engelsk godt, både muntlig og skriftlig.Krav til kompetanse i engelsk
Gode ferdigheter i engelsk er påkrevd for deltakelse i doktorgradsprogrammet. Internasjonale søkere må dokumentere dette med gyldig sertifikat fra en av følgende tester: 

• TOEFL - Test of English as a Foreign Language, Internet-Based Test (IBT). Minimum resultat: 90 
• IELTS - International English Language Testing Service. Minimum resultat: 6.5 
• Certificate in Advanced English (CAE) og Certificate of Proficiency in English (CPE) fra Universitetet i Cambridge 
• PTE Academic - Pearson Test of English Academic. Minimum resultat: 62 
Følgende søkere er fritatt fra ovennevnte krav: 

• søkere med ett års fullført universitetsstudier i Australia, Canada, Irland, New Zealand, Storbritannia, USA 
• søkere med fullført mastergrad med engelsk som undervisningsspråk i et EU-/EØS-land 
• søkere som er fritatt basert på HK-dir sin GSU liste Vi tilbyr
• doktorgradsutdanning ved et universitet med et tydelig samfunnsoppdrag og ambisiøse faglige mål
• et ambisiøst og inkluderende forskningsmiljø. Vi legger vekt på å involvere ansatte på alle nivåer i strategiske beslutninger og fremmer en uformell arbeidskultur med flat organisasjonsstruktur
• gratis norskopplæring dersom du ikke behersker norsk, svensk eller dansk på nivå A2 ved tiltredelse
• tilgang til Lifekeys, en digital tjeneste for mental helse og livskvalitet
• lønn etter Statens lønnsregulativ i stillingskode 1017 stipendiat, for tiden kr 580 000 brutto per år, med lønnsutvikling i ansettelsesperioden. Fra lønnen trekkes lovfestet innskudd til Statens pensjonskasse på 2 %
• medlemskap i Statens pensjonskasse med gode pensjons- og forsikringsordninger
Les mer om ansattgoder og fordeler på uis.no.
Mangfold
Mangfold er en styrke ved universitetet. Ulike erfaringer, perspektiver og bakgrunner bidrar til bedre løsninger og et godt arbeids- og læringsmiljø. Vi ønsker søkere med ulike kvalifikasjoner, livserfaringer og perspektiver, og oppfordrer alle kvalifiserte kandidater til å søke, uavhengig av kjønn, alder, funksjonsevne, kulturell bakgrunn eller om du har hatt opphold i arbeidslivet. UiS legger til rette for ansatte i ulike livsfaser og for medarbeidere med behov for individuell tilrettelegging. 
 
I tråd med gjeldende regelverk vil minst én kvalifisert søker med funksjonsnedsettelse, hull i CV-en eller innvandrerbakgrunn bli invitert til intervju. Dersom dette gjelder deg, kan du oppgi det i jobbsøkerportalen. Les mer om ordningen her.  
Har du spørsmål?
Vil du høre mer om stillingen, ta kontakt med:

Avdelingsleder: Hilde Alette Smedstad Moore, Tlf: 51832688, e-mail: hilde.s.moore@uis.no 

Har du spørsmål vedrørende rekrutteringsprosessen ta kontakt med: 

HR rådgiver: Elin Rødland, Tlf: 51832383, e-mail: elin.rodland@uis.no.
Søknaden
Søk stillingen elektronisk via «Søk stillingen» på denne siden. I Jobbnorge registrerer du søknad, relevant utdanning og arbeidserfaring samt språkferdigheter. I søknaden ber vi deg beskrive dine forskningsinteresser, din motivasjon for stillingen og hvordan din bakgrunn er relevant for forskningsprosjektet.

Følgende dokumentasjon skal lastes opp som vedlegg til søknaden:

Dokumentasjonen må foreligge på et skandinavisk språk eller engelsk. 

Søknaden vurderes på grunnlag av informasjonen som er registrert i Jobbnorge ved søknadsfristen utløp. Sørg derfor for at søknaden tydelig viser hvordan din kompetanse og erfaring oppfyller kompetansekravene i utlysningen, og at nødvendig dokumentasjon er lastet opp. Dersom vedleggene samlet overskrider 100 MB, må filene komprimeres før opplasting.

Stillingen er kunngjort på både norsk og engelsk. Ved eventuelle motstridende opplysninger mellom tekstene er det den norske teksten som legges til grunn.

jobs.description:
About the position
At the Centre for Precision Psychiatry, Institute of Clinical Medicine, University of Oslo, we have two full-time 3-year Postdoctoral Research Fellowships available within Novo Nordisk Foundation (NNF) funded projects focused on uncovering mechanistic links between mid-life metabolic trajectories and late onset Alzheimer’s disease (AD).

These positions offer an exciting opportunity for highly motivated researchers to work at the interface of multi-omics, brain and body imaging, and artificial intelligence, contributing to a large-scale Norwegian, UK, and international biobank collaborations aimed at understanding how midlife metabolic dysfunction shifts the risk and timing of AD.

These NNF funded projects collectively aim to uncover the molecular mechanisms linking midlife metabolic trajectories to late-onset AD, and to translate these insights into a novel explainable AI-driven multimodal framework for personalized prediction. The project integrates multi-omics data (genetics, proteomics, metabolomics), brain and body MRI, cognitive assessments, and health registry-linked data from individuals across Norway and the UK.

The Centre for Precision Psychiatry has access to a rich and unique data infrastructure, including large databases of biomarkers, clinical and cognitive variables, genotyping and sequencing data, and MRI brain imaging data from patients with neuropsychiatric and severe mental disorders. In addition, the Centre actively collaborates with major international consortia, including the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium (PGC), the ENIGMA consortium, and the European Alzheimer’s Disease DNA BioBank (EADB). The research environment further benefits from access to data from a broad range of national and international studies, including Norwegian population cohorts (e.g., DemGene, HUSK, HUNT, Tromsø study, and MoBa), UK-based cohorts (EPIC-Norfolk, Fenland, and the UK Biobank), the Estonian Biobank, and the ABCD and ADNI studies.
 
The positions are primarily focused on the development and application of statistical and machine learning methods for integrating large-scale longitudinal multi-omics data (proteomics and metabolomics), with clinical and imaging data, and genetics from Norwegian and international biobanks. The postdoctoral fellows will contribute to the following activities: (1) identifying midlife metabolic trajectories that precede neurodegeneration and AD, including metabolic subtyping; (2) linking these trajectories to established neurodegeneration markers, brain and body MRI, and cognition; (3) characterizing gene x environment interactions that shape AD risk and timing; and (4) developing and validating the “AD Avatar” for predicting age of onset.

The successful candidates will work closely with an interdisciplinary research environment including statisticians, geneticists, clinicians, and data scientists, and will conduct research using state-of-the-art secure infrastructure, including the TSD platform at the University of Oslo.

These postdoctoral fellowships are intended to strengthen the candidate’s scientific independence and publication record, and to provide strong qualifications for future academic or research leadership positions within precision medicine, population health, and data-driven neuroscience.

For more information: https://www.med.uio.no/klinmed/english/research/centres/precision-psychiatry/
Main responsibilities
• Analyze and integrate large-scale multi-omics data (affinity-based proteomics and NMR- and mass spectrometry-based metabolomics) from Norwegian and international biobanks, applying time-to-event models and advanced statistical and machine learning methods
• Develop and validate longitudinal models of metabolic trajectories and age-dependent genetic and environmental effects using in-house tools such as FEMA-LONG, and contribute to open-source analytical pipelines
• Apply Mendelian randomization, mediation, colocalization, and genetic overlap analyses (e.g., MiXeR, conjFDR) to investigate causal links between metabolic dysfunction, cardiometabolic disease, and AD-related outcomes
• Contribute to the development of the explainable “AD Avatar” predictive framework, including federated learning across Norwegian and UK-based data infrastructures (TSD, Tryggve, UKB-RAP)
• Collaborate with an interdisciplinary team and international partners in the UK, Sweden, Denmark, Iceland, Estonia, and the USA.
• Prepare and publish high-quality scientific manuscripts and present findings at national and international conferencesQualifications
Required

• A PhD in statistics, mathematics, informatics, genetics, medicine, psychology, or an equivalent field
• Strong programming skills in Python, R, or MATLAB, with emphasis on data analysis and method development
• Solid experience in statistical analysis and data processing using relevant statistical software
• Experience with large-scale human datasets, including multi-omics and/or imaging data
• Experience with tools and pipelines for genetic data analysis (e.g., PLINK, Regenie)
• Excellent proficiency in written and spoken English 
Preferred

• Experience with molecular quantitative trait loci studies, integrating NMR-based metabolomics (Nightingale) or mass spectrometry (Metabolon, Biocrates), and/or affinity-based proteomics data (SomaScan, Olink) with genetic data
• Experience with machine learning for large multimodal datasets and brain image analysis (e.g., FreeSurfer, FSL)
• Experience with computational methods and workflows for handling large-scale multimodal data
• Experience with survival analysis, longitudinal mixed-effects modelling, or clinical risk predictionPersonal skills
• Highly organized, self-driven, and goal-oriented, with strong productivity and attention to detail.
• Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary research teams.
